title: OpenAI Dumps Musk's Cursor, a Judge Guts the Pentagon's Anthropic Ban, and Sony Sues Claude's Maker
tldr: OpenAI is cutting Cursor off its models by Nov 12 after Elon Musk's SpaceX bought the coding tool — Musk says he "couldn't care less."
A federal judge ruled the Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic was unconstitutional retaliation, though Claude's government wind-down still finishes Sept 30.
Sony and Warner sued Anthropic over alleged copyright theft, naming CEO Dario Amodei personally as a defendant.

tips.heading: Ship an iOS app end-to-end with Codex
steps: Build a working app in Xcode, then give Codex the prompt below — it will build, archive, and distribute the app for you.
Have Codex open App Store Connect, sign in, and fill in your listing: description, screenshots, and the rest.
Complete the App Review contact, age-rating, and content-rights fields, checking each answer before continuing.
Set your price, click "Add for Review," fix anything flagged, then submit.
tips.prompt: Build this app and send it to App Store Connect.

tips.heading: Build a local file-converter with Claude before software gets retired
steps: Spot files locked into software that's about to disappear, e.g. Microsoft retires Publisher on Oct 1, 2026.
Tell Claude what you need: scan a folder for the file type, convert each one, save the output next to its source.
Ask Claude to also write a batch file so a less technical colleague can run it without touching PowerShell.
Ask Claude to turn the exchange into a reusable prompt template for the next software sunset.

news.body: OpenAI is cutting Cursor off its models by Nov 12, after Elon Musk's SpaceX bought the coding tool last month. OpenAI cites Musk's history of breaking agreements as the reason; Cursor's CEO says OpenAI models are only about 5% of Cursor's usage. Musk's response: "I couldn't care less."
news.means: Platform access from a rival lab can vanish overnight once ownership changes hands — worth building client-facing AI tooling with a fallback model in mind, not single-vendor lock-in.

news.body: A federal judge ruled the Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic as a "supply chain risk" was unconstitutional retaliation. Judge Rita Lin found the June designation, the first ever applied to a U.S. firm, violated the First and Fifth Amendments. The label stands pending appeal, and the Pentagon's wind-down of Claude finishes Sept 30 regardless.
news.means: A useful precedent if a client worries about a vendor being cut off for policy pushback — but Anthropic likely loses the government customer either way, so the legal win doesn't undo the commercial damage.

news.body: Sony Music and Warner sued Anthropic over alleged copyright theft, naming CEO Dario Amodei personally as a defendant. The suit calls it "one of the largest and most blatant" cases of AI training-data infringement to date.
news.means: Add this to the running list of AI copyright suits (OpenAI, Suno, Udio, now Anthropic) — worth flagging to any client evaluating AI-vendor legal exposure before a procurement decision.

beyond_ai.body: The U.S. secured a 100-year deal for access to more than a fifth of Venezuela's oil reserves, over 65 billion barrels across 17 fields. The private venture, led by Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt, becomes the world's second-largest corporate holder of proven oil reserves after Saudi Aramco; Venezuela's government says it brings tens of billions in investment and $209B in tax revenue, while Sen. Tim Kaine called it "corruption at epic scale."
beyond_ai.angle: A live case study in how fast energy-sector risk and opportunity can shift under a new political deal — relevant if any client touches energy, logistics, or Latin America market entry.
beyond_ai.starter: Did you see the U.S. just locked up a 100-year stake in Venezuelan oil? Curious how that shakes out for energy clients.

beyond_ai.body: Tim Cook's last day as Apple CEO was today; John Ternus, SVP of Hardware Engineering, takes over tomorrow. Cook stays on as executive chairman. Per Bank of America, Apple's market cap grew roughly $32 million per hour, every hour, across his 15 years leading the company.
beyond_ai.angle: A clean case study in planned succession at a company that famously avoided founder-dependency risk — a good reference point for a client's own leadership-transition planning.
beyond_ai.starter: Tim Cook just handed Apple to John Ternus after 15 years — what does our own succession plan look like if a key leader stepped back tomorrow?

beyond_ai.body: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launched Sunday on a SpaceX rocket, carrying a mirror repurposed from a donated spy satellite. Its field of view is over 100x wider than Hubble's and it captures data roughly 1,000x faster, generating about 1.4 terabytes a day hunting dark matter, dark energy, and exoplanets; first images are expected in early 2027.
beyond_ai.angle: No direct relevance to your work, general awareness only.
beyond_ai.starter: NASA just launched a telescope built from a recycled spy satellite mirror — wild what gets a second life in space.

beyond_ai.body: The economy unexpectedly lost 23,000 jobs in July; analysts expect a rebound of about 58,000 jobs when August's report lands Friday. Markets dipped Monday (S&P 500 -0.3%, Nasdaq -0.5%) after new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signaled rates could rise in September to fight inflation.
beyond_ai.angle: Directly relevant to budget and hiring conversations — a rate hike instead of a cut changes the calculus for any client planning fourth-quarter spend or headcount.
beyond_ai.starter: With the new Fed chair signaling a possible rate hike instead of a cut, are we still planning Q4 budgets around cheaper borrowing?

beyond_ai.body: Shiyazh Pete, an undrafted rookie offensive tackle, became the first member of the Navajo Nation to sign an NFL contract — even after being cut from the Dallas Cowboys' final roster. He received a standing ovation from fans during a preseason game and says he plans to keep pursuing an opportunity elsewhere.
beyond_ai.angle: No direct relevance to your work, general awareness only.
beyond_ai.starter: Did you catch the story about the first Navajo Nation player to sign an NFL contract? Great underdog story even though he didn't make the final roster.
